 This Appeal Coming On For Final Hearing This

Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

IA No.1/2025 is filed by the Insurance Company for receiving of the copy of the identity card,
Aadhar Card and Pan Card issued in the name of Kanthamma, as they disputed the date of birth of the deceased Kanthamma.
This court finds it reasonable to receive the said documents.
2. On perusal of the documents, it reveals that Kanthamma was born on 01.01.1972, as per the endorsement in the Pan Card.
NC: 2026:KHC:6911 HC-KAR 3.
Common award was passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.685 and 686 of 2021 and this appeal is filed to set aside the award passed in MVC No.686/2021 dated 13.06.2023 filed by the respondent/KSRTC 4.
Brief facts of the case are that the Kanthamma met with an accident on 24.01.2021 and died subsequently.
Her husband and children filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.45,60,000/-.
The tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.22,95,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from date of petition till realisation.

Divisional Controller vs Chikkanna on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60654481/
2 5.
Aggrieved by the said award, Insurance Company preferred this appeal and mainly contended that age of the petitioner was shown as 40 years as per Ex.P6/post mortem report.
Her elder son is aged 26 years and her husband is aged 50 years.
They had not produced aadhar card, voter ID card or pan card.
However, her date of birth as shown in the above documents is 01.01.1972.

Therefore,
her age is to be taken as 49 years and the NC: 2026:KHC:6911 HC-KAR multiplier as 13.

Hence,
requested for modification of the orders and the material documents are not available before the Tribunal, the Tribunal considered the age of the deceased as per post mortem report.
But the Insurance Company filed the copy of the Pan Card in which the date of birth of Kanthamma was mentioned as 01.01.1972 and she met with an accident on 24.01.2021.

As such, she was aged 49 years and the multiplier is to be taken as 13.
6.
Though it is stated that she was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, by doing milk vending business and flower business and earning Rs.35,000/- per month, she has not filed any income proof.
As she met with an accident in the year 2021, her notional income is to be taken as Rs.15,000/-as per the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
She is entitled for 25% towards future prospects and 1/3rd is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
The loss of dependency comes to Rs.18,750/- (15,000 + 25%) -1/3rd x 12 x 13 = Rs.19,50,000/-.

Petitioner No.1 is entitled NC:
2026:KHC:6911 HC-KAR for spousal consortium of Rs.44,000/-Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for an amount of Rs.44,000/- by each of them towards parental consortium.
They are also entitled for Rs.33,000/- under the conventional heads.
Amount Sl.Nos.

Particulars  in Rs.
 1 Towards loss of dependency 19,50,000  2 Towards loss of consortium 1,32,000  (3 claimants)
 3 Conventional heads 33,000

Hence, the compensation granted by tribunal is reduced from Rs.22,95,000/- to Rs.21,15,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
7.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award in MVC No.686/2021 dated 13.06.2023 on the file NC: 2026:KHC:6911 HC-KAR of the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Pandavapura, is modified.
